text: Manann was a folkloric figure in Irish folklore. The name was given to the pagan opponent of Saint Patrick. The saint was said to have chased Manann across the land and confined him to a pool in County Monaghan. Manann transformed into a bird, a hare, and a fish. Saint Patrick prayed that he would stay whatever he was until the end of time. Manann was a fish at that moment, so he never set fin outside the water again. Manann kept a great treasure in the pool, but no one could take it because of magical prohibitions. When people tried to drain the pool, fairies appeared and piped until the workers and the water began to dance, frightening the workers away. Manann has been described as a folkloric survival of the sea god Manannán mac Lir.
